text:
raj: Heads up — nightly backup restore for tenant=orion failed during decrypt with AccessDenied from KMS.
audit-bot: Alert: backup-restore-failure (tenant=orion) — KMSAccessDeniedException
raj: logs: 
```
2026-04-18T23:45:12Z restore: decrypt error: AccessDeniedException: User arn:aws:iam::123456:role/backup-executor is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/xyz-1234
```
maria: Did we change the key policy or add a deny anywhere? We rotated the backup-executor role name last week. @oliver any RBAC changes?
oliver: i pushed an IAM hardening update — tightened assume-role perms and scoped S3 access. i also applied a new KMS key policy snippet across backup CMKs to restrict cross-account grants per compliance ask.
sec-oncall: tagging sec & infra. this smells like key-policy + role rename coupling. recommend quick checks: 1) `aws kms get-key-policy` for the CMK 2) `aws iam get-role --role-name backup-executor` 3) CloudTrail lookup for kms:CreateGrant / kms:Decrypt events.
infra-bot: Detected: key policy update on alias/backups-main by infra-cfg-bot at 2026-04-17T07:12:33Z.
raj: running `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id xyz-1234` — policy includes a Condition restricting GrantCreation to principals where `aws:PrincipalAccount` == `123456` and denies `kms:CreateGrant` to `aws:PrincipalIsAWSService == false`.
maria: that deny looks similar to something we reviewed; might prevent our automation (grant rebind) from creating grants for the renamed role if the automation is not running as a service principal.
oliver: our role-rotation job runs in a CI worker which assumes a CI service role; CreateGrant is supposed to be created by that service role. but we also have a small lambda that rebinds grants and it runs as an assumed temporary session (not a service principal) — the new deny could block it.
sec-oncall: while we debug, can we do a scoped mitigation: create an explicit grant that allows Decrypt for the backup-executor role? that should unblock restores.
raj: prepared command: 
`aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/xyz-1234 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/backup-executor --operations Decrypt`
raj: created grant G-1a2b3c. restart restore job — testing now.
sec-oncall: verification?
raj: small snapshot restore succeeded. decrypt OK. marking as mitigated but will keep open for postmortem.
maria: followups from sec perspective: 1) audit all KMS key policies for denies on CreateGrant and special-case our automation paths 2) add unit/integration tests to role-rename pipeline to assert grants exist for new principals 3) hunt for leftover secrets that may have been exposed during role rename (we found one kube secret in staging last month).
oliver: noted. i'll roll back the overly-broad deny in the key policy and replace with a narrower allow for the CI service principal that runs grant rebinding. will add a comment in the policy to avoid accidental deletions.
infra-bot: CloudTrail sampling config shows KMS data events set to 100% for the `redwood-backups` key (changed by infra-cfg-bot 2026-04-18T00:12:00Z).
audit-bot: scanning for `kms:CreateGrant` events during role-rename windows... none found for the rename window (2026-04-17).
maria: we also discovered a stray file `/var/lib/backup/creds.tmp` on a legacy host during vuln-triage. raj, can you include creds rotation on the followup checklist?
raj: yes — rotating any ephemeral creds found and auditing for `/var/lib/backup/*` leftover files across fleet.
sec-oncall: postmortem action items (short):
- Revert/adjust key policy denies that block automation; add explicit allow for grant rebinder (owner: oliver)
- Add CI preflight: after role rename, script runs `aws kms list-grants` and fails the pipeline if new principal has no Decrypt grant (owner: maria)
- Add CloudTrail EventBridge rule: if `iam:UpdateRole` or role rename events occur, check for `kms:CreateGrant` or send an alert to sec-ops within 15min (owner: infra)
- Run infra-wide scan for leftover tmp credentials and rotate (owner: raj)
- Add runbook note: when changing CMK key policies, include a compatibility test with grant rebinder and backup agent (owner: sec-oncall)

maria: also: schedule a short blameless review with compliance to make sure key policy changes get a cross-team signoff.
oliver: will push policy tweak now and include the CI preflight hook in the rename pipeline.
sec-oncall: filing incident ticket SEC-2026-1222 with the tasks above.
audit-bot: Incident SEC-2026-1222 created and tasks assigned to owners.
raj: thanks — lesson: key policy hardening without validating automation paths can cause production restores to fail. keep automation principals in scope or provide an alternate rebinding path.
